proposals.rationale: Replaced meta-Br on aniline with F to reduce molecular weight/lipophilicity while retaining electron-withdrawing character, mimicking gefitinib-type halogen SAR.
Swapped Br for Cl at the meta position; smaller halogen often improves ligand efficiency in anilinoquinazoline EGFR inhibitors.
Replaced Br with nitrile as a polar bioisostere, potentially forming additional H-bond interactions in the EGFR back pocket.
Moved Br from meta to para position on the aniline ring to probe alternate vector into the hydrophobic pocket.
Extended one methoxy to a 2-methoxyethoxy chain (erlotinib-like) to improve solubility and explore the solvent-exposed region.
Introduced a basic dimethylaminoethoxy side chain in place of one methoxy to enhance aqueous solubility and potential for salt formation.
Replaced one ring methoxy with fluorine to reduce metabolic liability (demethylation) while retaining electronic effects on the quinazoline core.
Reconnected the quinazoline nitrogen substitution pattern (ring fusion isomer) to probe altered tautomeric/binding geometry while keeping same substituents.
Replaced one methoxy with a primary amine to introduce an H-bond donor and test alternate polarity in that region of the molecule.
Substituted methoxy with trifluoromethoxy to block oxidative O-demethylation and modulate electronics/lipophilicity.
